source_text: νέα, τὰ ἐπ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Προσιεμένη γὰρ οὐδαμῶς τὸν ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς νυμφίον, τοῖς τῶν Γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων προσέχει λόγοις. Γέγονε τοίνυν ἀνθρώπῳ ἀλλογενεῖ, καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀμέτοχος ταύτῃτοι μεμένηκεν· οὐ γὰρ ἔφαγε τὸν ἄρτον τὸν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι Χριστόν. Ὁρᾷς τὰ ἐγκλήματα, καὶ τὴν τοῖς τὰ τοιάδε δεδυσσεβηκόσιν ἐπενηνεγμένην εὐθὺς παρὰ Χριστοῦ δίκην. Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν καὶ τίνα τρόπον ἠλέηνται, καὶ ἀνεκομίσθησαν εἰς τὸ ἐν ἀρχαῖς· «Θυγάτηρ, φησὶν, ἱερέως, ἐὰν γένηται χήρα ἐκβεβλημένη, σπέρμα δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἐν αὐτῇ, ἐπαναστρέψει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῆς, κατὰ τὴν νεότητα αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἄρτων τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῆς φάγεται.» Χήρα μὲν γὰρ καὶ ἐκβεβλημένη διὰ τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν ἀσέβειαν, ἡ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀνεδείχθη Συναγωγὴ, καὶ μεμένηκεν ἐν ἁμαρτίαις, καὶ ἐν τῷ κεκτῆσθαι μηδὲν τῶν πνευματικῶν ἀγαθῶν, καὶ μακροὺς ἐν τούτῳ διατετέλεκε χρόνους. Ἀλλ' ἐπαναστρέψει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τὸν πατρικὸν αὐτῆς· κεκλήσεται γὰρ καὶ αὐτὴ διὰ πίστεως πρὸς Θεόν· ἐπιγράψεται δὲ σὺν ἡμῖν Πατέρα τὸν τῶν ὅλων δημιουργὸν, καὶ τῆς Χριστοῦ γένοιτ' ἂν εὐλογίας μέτοχος. Τοῦτό σοι σαφὲς τὸ μυστήριον καὶ ὁ τοῦ προφήτου καταστήσει λόγος· ἔφη γὰρ ὧδε· «Διότι ἡμέρας πολλὰς καθίσονται οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ, οὐκ ὄντος βασιλέως, οὐδὲ ἄρχοντος· οὐκ οὔσης θυσίας, οὐδὲ ὄντος θυσιαστηρίου, οὐδὲ ἱερατείας, οὐδὲ δήλων· καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπιστρέψουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐπιζητήσουσι Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν αὐτῶν καὶ βασιλέα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκστήσονται ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς αὐτοῦ, ἐπ' ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθὴς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐδώδιμα μὲν καὶ πρὸς μετάληψιν εὐπρεπῆ τοῖς ἀλωβήτως ἔχουσι τό γε ἐπὶ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς, τὰ ἱερὰ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὰ ἅγια. Προκείσεται δὲ οὐκέτι τοῖς οὐκ ἔχουσιν ὑγιῶς, ἢ σχέσει τῇ πρὸς ἑτέρους ἐκμεμολυσμένοις. Γέγραπται γὰρ, ὅτι «Μετὰ στρεβλοῦ διαστρέψεις.» Ὅτι δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἀληθῶς ἱεροῖς οὐκ ἀζήμιον τὸ ὡς ἐν χρήσει κοινῇ ποιεῖσθαι τὰ ἅγια, καὶ μηδὲν οἴεσθαι διενεγκεῖν τῶν ἄλλων αὐτὰ, διετράνου λέγων εὐθύς· «Καὶ ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἐὰν φάγῃ τὰ ἅγια κατ' ἄγνοιαν, καὶ προσθήσει τὸ ἐπίπεμπτον αὐτοῦ ἐπ' αὐτὸ, καὶ δώσει τῷ ἱερεῖ τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ οὐ βεβηλώσει τὰ ἅγια τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ἃ αὐτοὶ ἀφαιροῦσι τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἐπάξουσιν ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς ἀνομίαν πλημμελείας ἐν τῷ ἐσθίειν αὐτοὺς τὰ ἅγια αὐτῶν· ὅτι ἐγὼ Κύριος ὁ ἁγιάζων αὐτούς.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐ σφόδρα συνίημι ὅ τί ποτ' ἐστὶν ὃ φής. {ΚΥΡ.} Πεύσῃ τοι καὶ μάλα σαφῶς· ἄναντες γὰρ οὐδέν. Τὰ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀνατεθειμένα, μόσχοι τυχὸν, ἢ ὄϊς, ἀνεκομίζοντο μὲν ἐκ μέρους ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, ἐξαιρουμένων τῶν ἐντοσθίων, ποδῶν, τε καὶ κεφαλῆς, καὶ πιμελῆς, ἔσθ' ὅτε καὶ νεφρῶν· ἔτρεφον δὲ τοῖς λειψάνοις τοὺς ἱερεῖς. «Οἱ γὰρ ἐσθίοντες τὰς θυσίας, κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου εἰσὶ,» καθὰ καὶ ὁ θε
pass_a_gloss: [cont.] new (νέος), those upon Christ himself. For admitting (προσίημι) in no way the bridegroom (νυμφίος) from above and from God the Father, she gives heed (προσέχω) to the words of the Scribes and Pharisees. So she has become [wife] to an alien man (ἀλλογενής), and therefore has remained without share (ἀμέτοχος) of the holy things (τὰ ἅγια); for she did not eat the bread from heaven, that is Christ. You see the charges (ἔγκλημα), and the penalty (δίκη) brought at once from Christ upon those who committed such impiety (δυσσεβέω). Behold (ἀθρέω) now in what way they have been shown mercy (ἐλεέω) and restored (ἀνακομίζω) to what was at the beginnings. 'A priest's daughter, if she becomes a widow cast out (ἐκβάλλω), and seed (σπέρμα) is not in her, will return to the house of her father according to her youth, and will eat of the breads of her father' [Lev 22:13]. Widow and cast out because of the impiety (ἀσέβεια) toward Christ the Synagogue of the Jews was shown (ἀναδείκνυμι), and remained in sins, possessing none of the spiritual (πνευματικός) goods, and continued (διατελέω) long times in this. But she will return to her paternal house; for she too will be called (καλέω, fut. pf.) through faith (πίστις) to God; she will inscribe (ἐπιγράφομαι) with us as Father the craftsman (δημιουργός) of all things, and would become partaker (μέτοχος) of Christ's blessing (εὐλογία). This mystery (μυστήριον) the prophet's word will also establish (καθίστημι) clearly for you: 'For many days the sons of Israel will sit, there being no king nor ruler (ἄρχων), no sacrifice (θυσία) nor altar (θυσιαστήριον) nor priesthood (ἱερατεία) nor manifestations (δῆλοι); and after this the sons of Israel will turn back (ἐπιστρέφω) and seek (ἐπιζητέω) the Lord their God and their king, and will be astonished (ἐξίσταμαι) at the Lord and at his good things at the last of days' [Hos 3:4-5 LXX, without 'David']. PALL.: True the word. CYR.: So edible (ἐδώδιμος) and fitting (εὐπρεπής) for partaking (μετάληψις) to those who are unblemished (ἀλωβήτως) as far as depends on themselves are the sacred things, that is the holy things. But they will no longer be set before (πρόκειμαι) those not in sound state (ὑγιῶς), or polluted (ἐκμολύνω) by relation (σχέσις) to others. For it is written: 'With the crooked (στρεβλός) you will twist (διαστρέφω)' [Ps 17:27 LXX]. That even for those truly sacred it is not without penalty (ἀζήμιος) to treat the holy things as in common use (χρῆσις κοινή) and think them in no way to differ from the rest, he declared (διατρανόω) at once: 'And a man who eats the holy things in ignorance (ἄγνοια) will add its fifth part (ἐπίπεμπτον) to it, and give the holy thing to the priest; and he will not profane (βεβηλόω) the holy things of the sons of Israel which they set apart (ἀφαιρέω) for the Lord, and they will bring upon themselves lawlessness (ἀνομία) of trespass (πλημμέλεια) in their eating their holy things; for I am the Lord who sanctifies (ἁγιάζω) them' [Lev 22:14-16]. PALL.: I do not much understand what you say. CYR.: You will learn very clearly; for nothing is uphill (ἄναντες). The things dedicated (ἀνατίθημι) for an odour of fragrance (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας), calves perhaps or sheep, were carried up in part to the altar, the inwards (ἐντόσθια), feet and head and fat (πιμελή), sometimes also kidneys (νεφρός) being taken out (ἐξαιρέω); and they fed (τρέφω) the priests with the remains (λείψανον). 'For those eating the sacrifices are sharers (κοινωνός) of the altar' [1 Cor 10:18], as the divi- [cont. s.15].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …new charges, those that concern Christ himself. For she utterly refuses the Bridegroom who comes from above, from God the Father, and gives heed to the words of the scribes and Pharisees. So she has become the wife of a man of another race, and for that reason she has remained without a share in the holy things; for she did not eat the bread from heaven, that is, Christ (John 6:32). You see the charges, and the punishment that Christ at once brought on those guilty of such impiety. Now observe also how they have been shown mercy and been brought back to what they were at the beginning. ‘A priest’s daughter,’ he says, ‘if she becomes a widow, cast out, and there is no offspring in her, shall return to her father’s house as in her youth, and shall eat of her father’s bread’ (Leviticus 22:13). For the Synagogue of the Jews was shown to be a widow and cast out because of her impiety toward Christ; she has remained in sins, possessing none of the spiritual goods, and has continued so for a long time. But she will return to her father’s house; for she too will be called to God through faith; with us she will claim as Father the Creator of all things, and so would come to share in the blessing of Christ. The prophet’s words will make this mystery clear to you as well; for he spoke thus: ‘For the sons of Israel will remain many days without king or ruler, without sacrifice or altar, without priesthood or oracles; and afterward the sons of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and their king, and they will be filled with awe at the Lord and at his good things in the last days’ (Hosea 3:4–5).
Palladius: What you say is true.

Cyril: So the sacred things, that is, the holy things, are fit to be eaten and shared by those who, as far as it rests with themselves, are without blemish. But they will no longer be set before those who are not sound, or who have been defiled by their ties with others. For it is written: ‘With the crooked you will deal crookedly’ (Psalm 18:26). He made it plain at once that even for those who are truly consecrated it is not without penalty to treat the holy things as if they were for common use, and to think they differ in no way from other things; for he says: ‘And a man who eats the holy things in ignorance shall add a fifth more to it and give the holy thing to the priest; and he shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel which they set apart for the Lord, and they will bring on themselves the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things; for I am the Lord who sanctifies them’ (Leviticus 22:14–16).
Palladius: I do not quite understand what you mean.

Cyril: You will learn it very clearly; there is nothing hard about it. The offerings dedicated for a pleasing aroma, a calf, say, or a sheep, were carried up to the altar in part, once the entrails, the feet and head, the fat, and sometimes the kidneys too had been taken out; and with what remained they fed the priests. anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, completing s.13's 'ἀδελφὰ δὲ τούτοις καὶ / νέα'. Lev 22:13 again read with Cyril's 'χήρα ἐκβεβλημένη' and here 'σπέρμα … ἐν αὐτῇ'. Hosea 3:4–5 quoted from the LXX but without 'David' before 'their king' (LXX and Hebrew both have it); 'δήλων' is the LXX word for the Urim-type oracle (cf. Exodus 28:30 LXX δήλωσις), rendered 'oracles'; Hebrew has 'pillar … ephod or teraphim'. 'ἐκστήσονται' rendered 'filled with awe' (Hebrew: 'come trembling'). 'Μετὰ στρεβλοῦ διαστρέψεις' is LXX Psalm 17:27 = English Psalm 18:26 (also 2 Samuel 22:27); LXX sense 'with the crooked you will twist/deal crookedly'. Lev 22:14–16: Cyril reads 'οὐ βεβηλώσει' (he shall not profane) where the LXX has the plural; rendered as he has it; 'ἐπάξουσιν … ἀνομίαν πλημμελείας' kept close to the LXX. In 'ἐξαιρουμένων τῶν ἐντοσθίων …' Cyril does not say whether the parts taken out are those burned or those set aside; English keeps the same ambiguity. 'Pleasing aroma' (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας) is the standing Levitical formula, uncited. Section ends mid-word ('ὁ θε-'); s.15 completes 'inspired Paul said'.
